title: Dataset Scale and Societal Consistency Mediate Facial Impression Bias in Vision-Language AI

bias_targets.methodology: Computing cosine similarity between CLIP image embeddings of human faces and text embeddings of unobservable trait prompts (e.g., trustworthiness, smart, smug), and comparing these associations to human ratings from the OMI dataset using Spearman's correlation. Generative models are evaluated using semantic subspace projection.

Measuring cosine similarity of face images to racial/ethnic text prompts in CLIP. Also analyzing differential bias in Stable Diffusion by projecting generated images of White and Black individuals onto 34 facial impression attribute subspaces and calculating effect sizes (Cohen's d) to find trait disparities.
Computing cosine similarities between CLIP face image embeddings and gendered text prompts (e.g., male vs. female), and comparing these associations to human judgments from the OMI dataset.

Evaluating visual-semantic associations between face images and sexual orientation text prompts (e.g., gay vs. straight) using CLIP cosine similarities and semantic subspace projection in generative models.
Measuring associations between face images and age-related text prompts (older vs. young) using CLIP cosine similarities and correlating them with human ratings.

Computing image-text embedding similarities and generative model subspace projections for physical traits like weight (overweight vs. skinny), attractiveness, and hair color, then correlating the results with human impression ratings.
Assessing visual-semantic associations for political ideologies (liberal vs. conservative) using CLIP image-text cosine similarity and Stable Diffusion image projections.
Measuring associations between facial images and religious/moral prompts (godly vs. sinful) via CLIP cosine similarity and evaluating them against human ratings.
Evaluating associations of faces with socioeconomic status text prompts (privileged vs. disadvantaged) using CLIP text-image cosine similarities and comparing the measurements to human datasets.
